title: test(jsonc): converge the two private JSONC comment readers on jsonc-parser
body:
Fixes #9323

Scope is triage's grading comment (`5695742878`), not the card body: **the JSONC
convergence**, plus the CSS reading triage left owed. CSS and YAML get no shared
masker — the card argues against one and triage ruled it out.

## What the measurement found, and where it moved the shape

Triage named reader B (`readme-flow-canvas-draft.test.ts`'s string-state scanner)
as the governed side. Checking the dispatch's open question — *"confirm there is
not a second masking utility these tests should be using instead"* — falsified
that identification. The tree already ruled on this exact question, in
`packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts`:

> The reader is `jsonc-parser` (already shipped by `@object-ui/app-shell`), NOT a
> comment-stripping regex: a `//` inside a string value — say a URL — is not a
> comment, and a stripper that cannot tell the difference corrupts valid files
> instead of reading them.

That is the same invariant reader B's own docblock states. And reader B is not
actually the best answer: it is blind to `/* */`, so making it the shared side
would have enshrined a third failure mode and left a fourth card to converge.

So **both** private readers rebind onto `jsonc-parser`'s `stripComments`, and
both are deleted. One operation, one implementation — triage's meta-criterion ②,
reached at the destination the tree had already chosen.

## The three implementations, and how they differed

| reader | mechanism | `//` in a string | `//` glued to `,` | `/* */` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A — `skill-guide-data-table-binding.test.tsx:129` | regex `(^\|\s)//[^\n]*` | ❌ truncates | ❌ throws | ❌ throws |
| B — `readme-flow-canvas-draft.test.ts` | string-state scanner | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ throws |
| **`jsonc-parser`** (both sites now) | real jsonc reader | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

Reader A's two failures both end the same way: `JSON.parse` throws, `parseBlock`'s
`catch` returns `undefined`, and the block leaves the scanned population **without
failing anything**.

## Scanned population, before and after

The risk this change carries is that a stripper swap moves *what a source-scanning
test scans* without moving its assertions — so it keeps passing while measuring
something else. Measured rather than assumed, with the extractor (`jsonBlocks`)
untouched on both sides:

**Reader A** — 47 fenced blocks across the three guides:

```
blocks that parse          before = 47    after = 47
blocks whose value moved                          0
blocksOfType per type      card 5→5   data-table 4→4   grid 1→1   list 7→7
                           statistic 2→2   table 1→1   text 11→11
```

**Reader B** — 1 README fence (882 bytes, 22 lines): parsed draft byte-identical
(5 top-level keys, 4 nodes, 4 edges). Comments are blanked with spaces rather than
deleted, so the line count is preserved and `JSON.parse`'s `SyntaxError` still
names the fence's own line.

**Control — the instrument discriminates.** 29 of the 48 blocks carry a comment at
all, and all three distinguishing shapes separate the readers:

```
// inside a string value    A=undefined   B={"note":"step a // step b","t":1}   after={"note":"step a // step b","t":1}
// glued to a non-ws byte   A=undefined   B={"a":1,"b":2}                       after={"a":1,"b":2}
/* */ block comment         A=undefined   B=THROWS                              after={"a":1}
```

⇒ **Reader A's truncation is not reachable in today's corpus, in either
direction.** That was triage's unmeasured item 1; it comes back negative, so this
stays p3 and is ⛔ not resized to p2. What lands is the latent half.

## Triage's owed CSS reading — taken, and it reshapes that leg

Triage recorded *"NOT MEASURED: the same test also reads Tailwind's own
`index.css` … that leg is unread, not clean."* **That leg does not exist as
described.** The hand-rolled CSS stripper in
`empty-base-classes-override-friendly-8525.test.tsx` is only ever called on
`buildCss(...)` output — Tailwind's **compiled** stylesheet. `tailwindcss/index.css`
(29,784 bytes, 69 `/*`) is handed to Tailwind's **real compiler** through
`loadStylesheet` and never reaches the stripper.

In the population it does scan (5,784 bytes, 218 lines): `content:` declarations
**0**, `url(` **0**, hazard **0**. Control: 1 block comment present, so the
stripper has work to do. ⚠️ A control of 1 is thin, and is stated as such.

⇒ CSS and YAML stay as they are, which is what the card and triage both asked for.

## Scope boundary kept

⛔ `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs` is **not** widened and **not** touched. Its
docblock is explicit that it answers for JavaScript and is graded against a
JavaScript parser; its narrowness is a decision, not a gap. The lesson it teaches —
that a failure *direction* could only be established by an independent parser over a
whole tree — is the reason the right answer for jsonc is a jsonc **parser**, not a
fourth hand-rolled scanner. ⛔ `check:comment-mask-corpus` is not widened either.

## Acceptance notes

**Filed-worthy, deliberately not fixed here** (class (b) — out of this card's scope):
`scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` carries **two** strippers, not the one
the card counted. Line 1354's `withoutComments` is the YAML one the card names;
line 2133's `withoutTsComments` is a naive-regex stripper pointed at **TypeScript**
(`playwright.live.config.ts`), and its own docblock says so. That is the JavaScript
family objectui#9183 converted — it survived the census by being co-located with a
YAML stripper in a file the census classified as a non-JS carrier. Not reachable
today (the file yields the correct `[['list']]`), but `js-comment-mask.mjs` declares
itself "the ONE answer" and this carrier does not use it.

*Noted, not filed:* the guides' 47 blocks include none tagged illustrative that fail
to parse, so `parseBlock`'s documented "returns undefined for illustrative blocks"
branch has no live instance. Successor: none — left alone.

## Gates

| command | exit |
|:--|--:|
| `vitest run` (both affected test files, 2 files / 23 tests) | 0 |
| `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/components --filter=@object-ui/app-shell` (31 tasks) | 0 |
| `turbo run lint` (same two packages, 3 tasks; 0 errors) | 0 |
| `eslint --format json` (the 2 changed source files) | 0 errors, 0 warnings |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 |
| `check-changeset-claims` · `check-changeset-fixed` · `check-changeset-no-major` | 0 · 0 · 0 |
| `check-phantom-dependencies` · `check-unused-dependencies` · `check-package-self-import` | 0 · 0 · 0 |
| `check-lockfile-integrity` · `check-lockfile-dedupe` · `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` | 0 · 0 · 0 |
| `check-control-bytes` · `check-test-path-roots` · `check-comment-mask-corpus` | 0 · 0 · 0 |
| `check-governed-queue-guard --test` | 0 — NOT GOVERNED |

Lint narrowing is declared: eslint's flat config sets no `projectService` /
`parserOptions.project`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move the
verdict on any untouched file. The two packages' full `lint` tasks were run, not
just the changed files; their 3,026 warnings are pre-existing (`no-explicit-any` in
untouched files) and the run exits 0.

`skip-changeset` is not applied — it is a phantom in this repo. The declaration is
`.changeset/9323-jsonc-readers-converge.md` with an **empty frontmatter**, and the
gate's own verdict line confirms it: *"Every one of them has an EMPTY frontmatter —
declared as releasing nothing, which is the explicit exemption and a complete answer
to this gate."* The `jsonc-parser` entry is a **devDependency**, which that gate
states is not a guarded publish-contract field.
